clauses.mechanism: express revocation by EO 12148 section 5-106; effective July 15, 1979 by that order's own effective-date sentence (EO 12148 signed July 20, 1979)
clauses.reason: Whole order (single operative paragraph, offsets 889-1833 of the held Federal Register text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_10634.txt, 20 FR 6433): signed 1955-08-25; under the Defense Production Act of 1950, as amended, provides that, whenever financial assistance is not otherwise available on reasonable terms, loans (including participations and guarantees) under section 302 of that Act may be made to aid reconstruction, rehabilitation or replacement of facilities destroyed or damaged by a major disaster, when the facilities are required for national defense as determined by the Director of the Office of Defense Mobilization. No own-terms sunset or condition ends the order. Later orders EO 10773 (1958; list entry 14), EO 11051 (1962; section 601 list) and EO 11725 (1973; list entry 7) mention EO 10634 in enumerated lists of orders in orders that redirect references to, or authority of, successor mobilization and emergency-preparedness offices; they are later events about which office exercises the determination, and I found no language in them that revokes or terminates EO 10634 (the dossier lists their acting provisions as not located; I read the list entries in the held texts jobs/app-executive-orders/output/texts/executive-order-10773-delegating-and-transferring-certain-functions-and-affairs-the-office.txt, jobs/fr-originals/output/texts/EO_11051.txt and jobs/fr-originals/output/texts/EO_11725.txt, but did not read each of those orders end to end). First end: Executive Order 12148, Federal Emergency Management, section 5-106, which states that Executive Order 10634, as amended, relating to loans for facilities destroyed or damaged by a major disaster, is revoked; its closing section states that the order is effective July 15, 1979 (offsets 23765-23802 of the held text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12148.txt; the revocation sentence is at offsets 16364-16497). EO 12148 was signed 1979-07-20, so the effective date is retroactive by its own words; the first end is recorded on the stated effective date, 1979-07-15, with the signing date disclosed. No held source shows an earlier lapse of the Defense Production Act section 302 authority that the order invokes; that possibility is not excluded but is not supported by held evidence, and the order is permissive, so it is not treated as ended by disuse.

research_rationale:
EO 10634 authorizes Defense Production Act section 302 disaster loans for defense-required facilities, with the determination made by the Director of the Office of Defense Mobilization. The first held end is its express revocation by EO 12148 section 5-106, effective July 15, 1979 by that order's own words (signed July 20, 1979). Successor-office orders EO 10773, EO 11051 and EO 11725 redirect references or functions and are recorded as later events in the reason, not as ends. Searches: the U.S. Code and eCFR searches record two citation hits each for this order without a located text slice in the dossier, so they were not treated as evidence of continuation; the OFR disposition-note search lists the EO 12148 revocation.
